dek.en: A paper on how to price speed, Tarun Chitra on blockspace futures, a Wall Street evening in New York, Puffer joins the tests, and five role calls.

en: June answered a question the community had been asking since Flexnodes: if speed is worth money, who pays, and how much? Optimum’s answer was a paper. Every chain has a base lane, its normal way of moving data, and Optimum sells a fast lane on top, priced by the coded pieces a node buys to decode in time.

It took the idea to New York, where it co-hosted an evening on the new Wall Street being built on Ethereum, and to Tarun Chitra, who suggested the fast lane could one day become a futures market for blockspace.
Optimum published Speed is Money, research on pricing low latency: a base lane every chain has, and an RLNC fast lane priced per coded piece. Tarun Chitra discussed it for 50 minutes on YouTube.
Top of the Block in New York on 4 June brought 1kx, BitMine, Auros and Blockdaemon together before ETHConf. Puffer Finance joined as a mump2p testing partner.
Five role calls named 65 Refined members, the most of any month so far.

body.en: On 9 June Optimum summarised its new research on pricing latency, published on arXiv. Latency matters economically when information is only useful before a deadline. Every chain has a base lane, whether uncoded gossip, Reed Solomon or Raptor codes; Optimum’s fast lane adds RLNC pieces that raise the chance of decoding in time. The value is the gain in that probability, for example from 90% to near certainty, and the price is set per piece. Optimum said reliable on time delivery is what gives the fast lane its value.

On 2 June Optimum posted a 50 minute conversation with Gauntlet founder Tarun Chitra, who had joined its very first X Space in March 2025. Chitra looked at blockchains as repeated auctions and said that if Optimum’s Latency Marketplace works, it could give rise to futures markets for blockspace. Médard also spoke with David Lin about AI, quantum computing and blockchains on 3 June, and gave a talk on the math of post quantum security on 16 June.

title.en: Top of the Block in New York

body.en: On 4 June Optimum hosted Top of the Block, a pre ETHConf evening in New York with 1kx, BitMine, Auros and Blockdaemon about the institutional finance moving onto Ethereum. Kent Lin, Eli Laipson and Chandler Otterbein represented Optimum at ETHConf the following week, and on 9 June Optimum co-hosted a happy hour with OKX and Auros on agentic trading. Optimum’s line for the week: the market is the entire global financial system.

sources: Optimum on X, Top of the Block

body.en: On 17 June Puffer Finance became a mump2p testing partner. Asked a few days earlier whether a big name was coming, Optimum said only that onboarding was in progress with several key partners. On 22 June it published an interactive model, backtested on thousands of slots, estimating how much extra revenue a validator would earn with mump2p’s speed advantage. With 3 million ETH waiting to enter staking, Optimum argued, demand from institutions was real.
Flash posted a role call every week of June, on 1, 8, 15, 23 and 29 June, naming 65 new Refined members in all, the most in any month since the role calls began. Each of them is listed below.

title.en: A new product lead, and a data scientist wanted

body.en: On 5 June Optimum welcomed Lewej Whitelow, who leads protocol development and releases on the product side. On 30 June it opened a senior data scientist role working across networking infrastructure, decentralized systems and empirical blockchain research. A thread on 8 June looked ahead to Glamsterdam, Ethereum’s next upgrade, and what enshrined proposer builder separation means for slot timing.
